proposal_sample.reason: The label is the paper's title on page 1. Class Investigation with current lineage fits target entities-01, which describes the current documentary investigation rather than a single executed test. One flaw: the third support quote is reference [2] on page 19 (the Beeson et al. ASTM handbook). That is a cited work, not this investigation, so it should be dropped from support. It does not change the entity's identity. (same assertion as judged proposal c629e511)

Brass-filled PTFE is the central material of the paper. Page 2 says MCRF is 'currently testing' it, and the Table 1 row carries footnote b (NASA-STD-6001), which marks MSFC data. Class Material and current lineage are right. The entity is the material, kept separate from the Batch #1-#4 samples and from Salox-M. It says nothing about the brass fraction, which the paper states is unknown (page 10), so it fits target entities-03. (same assertion as judged proposal b4a070bc)
TFE-Teflon® (PTFE) as a current comparator: Table 2 prints a footnote-b row (NASA-STD-6001 MSFC), so current lineage is defensible.

Algoflon is a real named material: page 2 lists it as a compared polymer. Current lineage is right, because page 11 says two types were 'tested at the same conditions' and Table 3 rows are footnote a, 'NASA-STD 6001 MSFC'. This entity is only the family name, however. The tested materials are Algoflon E2 and Algoflon F7, which are accepted separately and gave opposite LOX results: E2 had 0/20 at 10,000 psia, while F7 failed at 10,000 psia and passed only at 5,000 psia. No E2 or F7 outcome may be attached to this generic entity (targets entities-05 and -06). Its only support is the page 2 list.

Salox-M is a distinct material that MSFC tested in this work. Page 2 says it 'was tested in comparison to Brass-filled PTFE', and its Table 3 rows are footnote a, 'NASA-STD 6001 MSFC'. Page 10 defines it as bronze-filled PTFE (40% bronze, 60% PTFE), so class Material with current lineage is right. It stays separate from Brass-filled PTFE, as target entities-04 expects. The 40% composition belongs to Salox-M only and must not be read as the brass fraction of Brass-filled PTFE, which is unknown. (same assertion as judged proposal 664dda6f)
Algoflon E2, tested at the same conditions (p11).
Algoflon F7, tested at the same conditions (p11).
Kel-F 81 marked cited; its data are cited (Chou/Giedorowicz, [4]).
p10 Bronze, the filler of Salox-M, as a current Material (same assertion as judged proposal c6bffd19).
Brass, the filler of the Brass-filled PTFE tested here, as a current Material (p10 "the percentage of Brass in the Brass-filled PTFE is not known").

Table 3 on page 12 defines Batch #1 as a real tested cohort with four condition rows (LOX 0/20, GOX 0/20, LOX 4/80, GOX 0/80), all marked footnote a = NASA-STD 6001 MSFC. That makes it current MSFC specimens, not a single invented run. Sample is the closest class: the ontology has no Batch class, and Sample keeps it distinct from the Brass-filled PTFE Material. The leading 'a' in the label is the footnote marker, not part of the material name. It should be normalized or kept as a provenance annotation, but it does not change the subject. The page 9 conflict (no reactions in 80 vs 4/80) concerns observation rows and must stay unresolved at that level; it does not affect this entity. (same assertion as judged proposal 18d0118e)

Batch #2 is real. Page 10 says a second batch was tested under the same conditions to check batch-to-batch variability, and Table 3 gives it its own rows (GOX 0/20, LOX 1/60, MSFC footnote a). Sample and current are appropriate, and it stays distinct from Batch #1, as entities-08 requires. The support snippet is the same truncated page 12 text, cut off at 'aBrass-fill', so it never shows '(Batch #2)'. The page itself confirms the label, so this is a weak-evidence issue, not a wrong subject. The 'a' prefix is a footnote marker. (same assertion as judged proposal 8846b16a)

Page 10 says two additional batches were tested at the same conditions with zero reactions. Table 3 lists Batch #3 with GOX 0/20 and LOX 0/20 at 98 J, 10,000 psia (MSFC footnote a). So it is a real current sample cohort, and Sample is appropriate. The support snippet is truncated before the batch number, but page 12 contains the label. The 'a' prefix is a footnote marker. (same assertion as judged proposal c056d2b0)

Batch #4 is the second of the 'two additional batches' on page 10. In Table 3 its GOX 0/20 row is on page 12 and its LOX 0/20 row continues on page 13. It is a real current MSFC cohort (footnote a), and Sample is appropriate. The support covers only the truncated page 12 header, which shows neither '(Batch #4)' nor its page 13 row. The source still confirms the entity, so this is non-critical. The 'a' prefix is a footnote marker. (same assertion as judged proposal c4360f12)

Conditional pass/fail criterion typed Requirement/normative_requirement; verbatim p6 sentence; matches target statements-23.

Verbatim page 18 conclusion. It names MCRF/MSFC research and Brass-filled PTFE, so author_reported_conclusion with current lineage and the investigation as subject is right. The claim of 'all of the positive characteristics' is an author evaluation. Labelling it a conclusion rather than a measured observation keeps it separate from the mixed impact data (4/80 LOX in Batch #1, 1/60 in Batch #2).

Verbatim page 18 author synthesis about low heat of combustion, elevated AIT and very high mechanical-shock resistance in LOX/GOX. As an author_reported_conclusion with current lineage it is correctly attributed. Classed this way, it doesn't promote the censored AIT (>425 C) to an exact value or erase the LOX reactions in Table 3 (4/80, 1/60). The suitability wording stays the authors' evaluation, not a normative requirement.

This matches target statements-29: an author conclusion on page 18 about the choice and percentage of filler, not a causal mechanism the assistant inferred. The role (author_reported_conclusion) and current lineage are right. Reviewers should note that the source says the Brass percentage is unknown (page 10), so the filler-percentage claim rests on the Salox-M comparison (40% bronze). That is correctly left as the authors' claim.

This matches target statements-30: the authors' comparison on page 18, similar to TFE-Teflon in high-pressure LOX and far better in high-pressure GOX. The LOX/GOX distinction is preserved. 'Best choice for oxygen systems' stays labelled as author_reported_conclusion, not normative_requirement and not an assistant recommendation, which is the right role. Current lineage is right for the conclusion itself, even though the TFE-Teflon comparison rows come from KSC (Table 5) and WSTF/MSFC (Table 6).
